source_text: eos non hoc intuitu operam dedisse propagini, ut tamquam reos gignerent filios Baptismate diluendos, eo quod Baptisma quo nunc adoptamur nondum fuerat institutum
pass_a_gloss: Them not this intuitu operam dedisse propagini, so-that/as tamquam guilty gignerent sons in-baptism diluendos, to-that that/which baptism whither now adoptamur not-yet fuerat institutum.
pass_b_english: The ancient holy fathers did not devote themselves to producing offspring with the intention of generating guilty children to be cleansed by baptism, because the baptism through which we are now adopted had not yet been instituted.

choices.why: Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
